candidates.change_summary: Replace require(msg.sender == Owner) with require(msg.sender != Owner) to allow anyone except the Owner to call withdraw.
Delete the require statement so anyone can call withdraw, not just the Owner.
Change the transfer recipient from Owner to msg.sender, so the sender gets the balance instead of the Owner.
Convert the transfer call to a low-level call that sends the entire balance to the Owner and then reverts, so the Ether is always sent but the transaction always fails.

Insert a zero-value transfer to the Owner before the actual balance transfer, causing the balance to be drained twice (first with zero, then with the remaining) and potentially altering the final balance state.
Delete the entire body leaving only the function signature, so withdraw does nothing and does not transfer funds.
Remove the owner-only require check so anyone can call Command.
Replace the low-level call with a no-operation (no code) so the external call never happens.
Insert a selfdestruct that destroys the contract after the call, so subsequent Command calls revert.
Replace the require check that asserts no overflow with an always-failing require(false) so the transfer never occurs and multiplicate behaves differently.
Remove the if condition guard so the transfer always executes when msg.value is zero, changing when multiplicate attempts a transfer.
Change the transfer amount from address(this).balance+msg.value to just address(this).balance, altering the final balance change of the contract and the recipient.
Change the recipient of the transfer from the function argument adr to Owner, so funds go to a different address and the contract's subsequent multiplicate behavior changes.
Change the if condition from msg.value>=address(this).balance to msg.value>address(this).balance, which changes the edge case when they are exactly equal and thus alters transfer behavior.
Delete the require statement that checks for overflow, so when overflow would occur the transfer still executes but potentially with a lower amount due to wrapping, changing the final state.
